topic: May an agent edit build/*.py to comply with "fix the generators"? Seven issues wait on this one line.
question: House rule 2.2 bars every seat in this company from editing build/*.py. Clean publishing, part 2 (2026-09-26) says "fix the generators, not only the pages", and the generators are build/*.py. The two are standing rules of equal standing pointing opposite ways, so no seat can pick a winner under rule 3.1, and no agent ruling can settle it either: the bar is in the agent instructions, and changing a policy is barred outright by rule 6. Which reading governs?
sides: AGENTS.md, house rules 2.2: "Touch only files the task needs. Never edit: sources/ (read-only, always), CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, BRIEF.md, ROADMAP.md, schema/, build/*.py, build/*.sh, .claude/, .mcp.json, .gitignore, desktop/, bot/ code..."
AGENTS.md, "Clean publishing, part 2: no provenance, no self-mention (2026-09-26)": "The table's generated pages (State of Play, Fronts) follow this too: fix the generators, not only the pages."

Precedent both ways: eceea52 fixed three generators in build/table.py, committed by Isaac, not by an agent. 0ed20a4 (WAR-36, build/voices.py) is the one agent commit that crossed the bar, on Isaac's word at the time; CONTINUE.md:430-433 records that contradiction as unsettled.

What waits on it: WAR-55, WAR-97, WAR-101, WAR-104, WAR-112, WAR-121, WAR-158, WAR-159 -- seven issues and the MCP's twelve writing tools. CONTINUE.md:454: "Settle the build/*.py wall first." Every patch is already written and verified; WAR-159's is reports/clean-publishing-generators.patch (3 files, 5 hunks, git apply --check clean, all three files compile).

options.label: a. The bar holds. build/*.py stays Isaac's alone; agents diagnose and hand over a verified patch, and he applies it.
options.changes: Nothing in the rules changes. The seven issues stay parked until he applies each patch by hand. reports/clean-publishing-generators.patch is ready now and is one git apply.

options.label: b. Narrow carve-out: an agent may edit build/*.py only where a standing rule names the fix (clean publishing's "fix the generators"), string-level changes only, no logic, reviewed before push.
options.changes: WAR-158 and WAR-159 ship this week. The other five (WAR-55, 97, 101, 104, 112, 121) are logic fixes and stay parked, because they change behaviour rather than a printed string.

options.label: c. Lift the bar for build/*.py generally, keeping it on sources/, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, schema/ and .claude/, with a review stage on every build/ change.
options.changes: All seven unpark. AGENTS.md 2.2 drops build/*.py and build/*.sh from the never-edit list and gains a review requirement; the MCP's twelve writing tools get fixed from inside the company.

options.label: d. Something else -- say it and it becomes the rule.

topic: The non-force ladder is keyed to Part Eleven's Passive Pressure Field column. Confirm that reading, or give authority radius its own scale.
question: Card 1 Q8 asked for a second Range ladder for addressing range, authority radius and anchor reach, keyed to Grade. Rather than invent a scale, the published ladder reads Part Eleven's existing Passive Pressure Field column as the authority radius at reference density (the radius where a practitioner's field still stands above the ground's is exactly a pressure-balance boundary), and puts anchor reach one decade inside and addressing range one decade outside it. That is one derivation step carrying the whole ladder: if the reading is wrong, every figure moves together. Is the Passive Pressure Field the authority radius, or should authority radius be laddered separately?
sides: "| A | Sky hums within 200 m |" and "| S | Storm reverence within 1 km |" - wiki/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/III. Physical Force (Part Eleven).md:109-124, the Passive Pressure Field column

"Aura Pressure is the passive force a character's metaphysical presence exerts on everything in proximity. Not a technique." - same file:127, which describes the column as presence rather than as jurisdiction

"Governed primarily by Harmonics, particularly Attunement and Projection, with secondary contribution from Dominion's Pressure" - same file:131; the ladder as published makes a Harmonics-governed radius carry Dominion's authority

options.label: Keep the reading. The Passive Pressure Field is the authority radius at reference density, and the other two reaches are one decade either side of it.
options.changes: Nothing moves; the published ladder stands, and no new scale enters the system.

options.label: Ladder authority radius separately, off Dominion Sovereignty or Dominion Radius rather than off the Passive Pressure Field.
options.changes: The whole non-force ladder is rebuilt and republished; a Sub-Stat-keyed ladder does not key to Grade, so the answer to card 1 Q8 changes shape.

options.label: Keep the reading but scale authority radius down by a stated factor, on the grounds that being felt is cheaper than holding jurisdiction.
options.changes: All three columns shift by that factor; the terrain multipliers, the B-Grade crossover and the Wellspring Core figure all move with them.

topic: Does the em-dash ban (R15-1) govern system-page documentation, or only scene prose? The published wiki does not currently meet it.
question: build/verify.py enforces the AI-tell checks on anything it is pointed at, and R15-1 says they are about prose failing rather than about period. House rule 4.2 requires every FAIL fixed on prose an agent writes. The thirteen bodies published under this issue were rewritten without em dashes and all thirteen PASS, but the system pages they were inserted into are full of em dashes already, so a reader sees one register in the old paragraphs and another in the new ones. A related case: the Counterplay bullet's own canon clause fails the antithesis check on its own, unchanged, and was preserved verbatim rather than rewritten, because rewriting another page's live sentence is not this issue's scope.
sides: "The AI-tell checks. Em dashes, similes, not-X-but-Y, countdown negation, gloss, ladder. These are about prose failing, not about period." - RULINGS.md, R15-1-AI_TELL_CHECKS_SURVIVE, quoting Pack Fifteen §1

"**Essence** · Personal Aether — drawn into the soul, circulated through the Soul Crystal, and imprinted with the practitioner's identity." - wiki/The Magic System/The Core Vocabulary.md:43, one of many live em dashes on the page this job wrote into

"**The counter-Fulguria kit has been leather and ceramic for four centuries and it is not a secret; it is simply cheaper to ignore until somebody dies of it.**" - wiki/The Magic System/Counterplay What Beats a Practitioner.md:25, live canon that fails the antithesis check

options.label: The checks govern scene prose only. System pages, glossaries and registers are exempt, and verify.py is not the gate for them.
options.changes: New system-page text may use the wiki's existing register; nothing already published needs touching.

options.label: The checks govern everything published. The existing wiki is out of compliance and gets a sweep of its own.
options.changes: A large sweep over the wiki's em dashes and antithesis clauses, as its own job; new text keeps meeting the checks as this job's did.

options.label: The checks govern everything an agent writes from now on, and existing text is left alone.
options.changes: What this job already did becomes the standing practice: new paragraphs meet the checks, inherited sentences are preserved verbatim and reported.

topic: The AU/s ladder against the cards: which gives way?
question: Card 1 q2 asked for an AU/s progression by Stage and said 'correct cards that miss it'. R44-5's operative sentence says the card governs per character and the tables are typical ranges, and your first rule for ruling says a ruling's general sentence reaches every case it describes. 23 of 29 attested AU/s figures sit outside their Stage's band. Which wins?
sides: "an AU/s progression by Stage (or Tier of Standing); correct cards that miss it" — WAR-3 card 1 q2, RULINGS.md 2026-09-26
"The card's eta governs per character and the tables are typical ranges; an in-world-acknowledged outlier is lawful." — R44-5, RULINGS.md 2026-09-25
"The formula governs: AU/s = Flux Density x eta." — R44-2, RULINGS.md 2026-09-25, which makes any AU/s correction force a second edit to Flux Density
WAR-102 set AU/s by hand for Gimbzo (8.6 million), Dougou (3,900 external), Elion and Sodoku; two of those sit outside the new band

options.label: The ladder is typical ranges; cards stand (what is published now)
options.changes: Nothing moves. The 23 misses stay listed in reports/essence_scales_2026-09-26.md as outliers.

options.label: Correct every miss to its Stage's benchmark AU/s, recomputing Flux Density from AU/s / eta so the formula still holds
options.changes: 23 cards change. Every card at the same Stage lands on the same AU/s figure, which is the collapse C-059 was written to avoid for EU.

options.label: Scale each card by one factor as C-059 does for EU: factor = benchmark / stated, applied to every AU/s figure on the card
options.changes: 23 cards change, within-card distinctness kept, across-card distinctness lost at the anchor figure. Cards with a hand-set WAR-102 figure are exempt.

options.label: Only correct cards that also fail AU/s = Flux Density x eta
options.changes: 12 cards change; the rest stand as outliers.

topic: Does the EU unit carry a floor at the bottom of the ladder?
question: At 1 EU = 1 MJ the EU-by-Stage table makes a Murmuring practitioner's whole reserve a fraction of one EU (band 3.000x10^-4 to 1.500x10^-2, benchmark 2.121x10^-3), and Welling's benchmark is 0.5602 EU. Ascension upward is fine (147.9 EU). The figures are published as computed. Should the unit hold a floor, or do Initiates genuinely deal in thousandths of an EU?
sides: "One constant: 1 EU = 1 MJ stands." — R44-1, RULINGS.md 2026-09-25
"| E | 26-50 | 300 J - 15 kJ |" — Part Four, wiki/Fracture of Worlds - The Living System/II. Grades, Gates and Thresholds (Parts Four-Ten).md
Cards at low Stage state thousands of EU: Yukazuri Moto 3,100 EU at Stage IV, Naori Yukari 42,000 at Stage III, Dorrik 1,840

options.label: Leave it: a fraction of an EU at Stage I and II is the honest reading (what is published now)
options.changes: Nothing. Low-Stage card figures then read far above their band and become corrections in their own pass.

options.label: Floor the unit at 1 EU and state that Stages I and II are measured in whole EU by convention
options.changes: The two bottom rows of the table are rewritten; the low-Stage card figures still miss, by less.

options.label: Re-scale the constant so Stage I lands at a countable reserve
options.changes: R44-1 is reopened, and every figure in the Essence Ledger and on twelve scaled cards moves with it.
